acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Just one box of a specially enriched peanut butter paste can save the life of a severely malnourished child. So why have 500,000 of those boxes been stuck in warehouses in Rhode Island?

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
USAID was founded in 1961. Since then, it has spent hundreds of billions of dollars all over the world. What did that get us? Producer David Kestenbaum talked with Joshua Craze and John Norris about that.
Joshua Craze's article for the New York Review of Books is " USAID: Goodbye to All That? " John Norris wrote the book The Enduring Struggle - The History of the U.S. Agency for International Development and America’s Uneasy Transformation of the World.
acts.title: 63 Years, 7 Months, 26 Days

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Two Americans moved to Eswatini when that country was the epicenter of the AIDS epidemic. With support from USAID, they built a clinic and started serving HIV+ patients. Now that US support for their clinic has ended, they are wondering if what they did was entirely a good thing.
Chico Harlan wrote about USAID in Eswatini for The Washington Post.
acts.credits: By Diane Wu and Chico Harlan
acts.title: Case Study

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc:
When USAID suddenly stopped all foreign assistance without warning or a transition plan, it sent people all over the world scrambling. Especially those relying on daily medicine provided by USAID. Producer Ike Sriskandarajah spoke to two families in Kenya who were trying to figure it out.
Katharine Houreld wrote about cuts to PEPFAR in Kenya for The Washington Post.
acts.title: Two Daughters
